title: From Transformer to Vision Transformer (ViT)
reading: The slide presents the Vision Transformer as a building block for vision foundation models: images are cut into sequences of patches and a standard Transformer is applied over those patches. It stresses that this yields a unified architecture usable across language, vision, and audio/3D/other sequence modalities. The canonical ViT architecture figure from Dosovitskiy et al. accompanies the text, and the paper is cited at the bottom.

visuals.description: ViT architecture: an image split into a 3x3 grid of patches, flattened and passed through a Linear Projection of Flattened Patches, producing tokens 1–9 plus an extra learnable [class] token 0, each combined with a patch+position embedding; these feed a Transformer Encoder whose class-token output goes to an MLP Head producing class labels (Bird, Ball, Car, ...).
visuals.assertion: An image can be treated as a token sequence: patch embeddings plus position embeddings feed a standard Transformer encoder, and a prepended learnable class token's output drives classification via an MLP head.

concepts.name: Vision Transformer (ViT)

concepts.name: Patch + position embedding
